name: Field
summary: The wrapper that stacks a label, a control, a hint and an error message, plus fieldset and legend for groups.
description:
Every form control sits in a .v-field so the label, help text and error line up the same way everywhere. Client-side errors show only after the person has used the field (:user-invalid), so a fresh form never opens in red.

Use a .v-fieldset with a .v-legend for a group of related fields or choices, and .v-fieldset-plain when the group should not draw a box.

classes.name: v-field
classes.description: Stacks label, control, hint and error with an even gap.

classes.name: v-label
classes.description: The field label. Use a real <label for> so clicking it focuses the control.

classes.name: v-required
classes.description: The red asterisk in a label. Decoration only, mark it aria-hidden and put required on the control.

classes.name: v-optional
classes.description: A quiet "Optional" note pushed to the end of the label row.

classes.name: v-hint
classes.description: Help text under the control, linked with aria-describedby.

classes.name: v-field-error
classes.description: The error message, hidden until the control is invalid. Always shows an icon, never colour alone.

classes.name: v-fieldset
classes.description: A boxed group of fields with a legend.

classes.name: v-fieldset-plain
classes.description: A fieldset that only groups (checkboxes, radios) and draws no box.

states.description: After the person has interacted with an invalid control, its .v-field-error shows. Nothing shows on a fresh form.
Server-side error: the message is always visible. Link it with aria-describedby on the control.
What assistive tech reads as required. The asterisk is only a visual cue.
Points the control at its hint (and at a server error), so they are read after the label.

a11y: Every control needs a visible <label for>, placeholder text is not a label.
For client-side errors keep the message out of aria-describedby: the browser already announces the invalid state. For server errors, set aria-invalid="true" and link the message.
Error messages carry an icon and the invalid control gets a doubled border, so state never depends on colour alone.
Group checkboxes and radios in a <fieldset> with a <legend>, so the question is read with each option.
